history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: Gopachal Parvat is a Jain site. Religious affiliation is confirmed as Jainism (Digambara sect) by Wikipedia's infobox and all consulted sources. It comprises gigantic rock-cut Jain carvings around the walls of Gwalior Fort - the most extensive series of Jaina caves known to exist anywhere, in the words of James Burgess. About 18 colossal Tirthankara statues (2-14 m tall) in seated Padmasana and standing Kayotsarga postures adorn the cliff face; the most prominent is a 47-foot Parshvanatha idol in lotus posture. Per Jain tradition, Parshvanatha delivered his spiritual discourse (deshna) on this hill, and one source calls it a Siddha Kshetra. The complex also includes 26 Jain temples on the hilltop and at the base (per evendo.com; verify). The statues were defaced in 1527 on Babur's orders (recorded in the Baburnama as the mutilation of the Urvahi Jinas); the Jain community later restored them by adding stucco heads. The site is now an ASI-protected Adarsh Smarak Monument. 'Gopachal' means 'Cowherd Mountain'. CSV town and state ('Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh') are correct.
